primaryStatutoryAuthority.description: A person seeking to seal more than one record may petition the district court for the county, which may seal all the records within that county including justice and municipal court cases. This is a venue overlay on the conviction and non-conviction sealing sections rather than a separate remedy: each underlying record must still satisfy its own section.

Conviction sealing. A verified criminal history from the Nevada Central Repository is a statutory attachment under NRS 179.245(2)(a). Eligibility turns on the offence category — category A through E felony, gross misdemeanour or misdemeanour — and on whether the offence is a crime of violence.
Sealing where the proceedings did not result in a conviction. A verified criminal history from the Nevada Central Repository is a statutory attachment under NRS 179.255(3)(a).

On sealing, the proceedings are deemed never to have occurred and civil rights are restored. NRS 179.295 allows sealed records to be reopened and NRS 179.301 allows certain persons and agencies to inspect them.

counselFlags: Record sealing, never expungement. The Nevada Department of Public Safety states directly that sealing is not expungement because it does not authorise destruction of the records.
Sealing does not restore firearm rights. Only a pardon that does not restrict the right to bear arms does.
Nevada orders do not bind out-of-state agencies and do not reach federal, tribal, military or out-of-state records.
Consolidation changes the venue, not the eligibility: each individual record must itself satisfy NRS 179.245 or NRS 179.255. Any record that does not qualify defeats its own inclusion.
Records in more than one county need separate petitions in each county's district court; this Petition reaches only records held within a single county.

Prosecutor stipulation is obtained before filing, and the prosecuting agency's position is never asserted by LegalEase. Clark County practice: the district attorney will not stipulate to petitions that include municipal court matters, so the packet goes to the appropriate city attorney and then to the district attorney with a separate signature line for each prosecuting agency. Prosecutor refusal to stipulate converts the matter into a contested hearing and ends self-help.

Nevada verification: the source establishes that the petition, declaration and verification are signed by hand, but it does not identify a verification or notarization statute for the NRS 179.2595 petition. Confirm the required verification form with counsel and the clerk before filing; the source does not specify one.
Filing fee: the source does not establish a filing fee for an NRS 179.2595 consolidated petition. No fee amount may be stated to a participant; confirm with the clerk of the district court.

Waiting period: the source does not establish an independent waiting period for the consolidated petition itself. Each underlying record carries the waiting period of its own section, which turns on the offence category and on whether the offence is a crime of violence — a legal classification driving a one-year versus ten-year answer.

Any offence-category question, any pending charge, any conviction during the clean period other than a minor moving or standing traffic violation, and any packet mixing municipal court matters with justice or district court matters end self-help and require attorney review.
Handwritten signature is mandatory on the petition, declaration and verification: Las Vegas Municipal Court treats typed signatures as cause for immediate denial.

certificate_of_service.detail: Absent by design: Nevada's vehicle is prosecutor stipulation obtained before filing, not service of process by the participant. The packet goes to the prosecuting agency first and is filed with the clerk only after the prosecutor stipulates, so the source prescribes no participant certificate of service.

notice_affidavit.detail: Blocked, not drafted. The Nevada packet requires an affidavit or declaration in support and a stipulation carrying a separate signature line for each prosecuting agency. The source does not reproduce the text or required contents of either instrument, and the stipulation records the prosecuting agency's position — a position LegalEase must never assert. Recorded as a dependency instead of drafted.

filing_instructions.detail: Obtain the verified criminal history from the Central Repository first, submit the packet to the prosecuting agency for stipulation, then file with the clerk of the district court and serve the signed order on each named agency. The filing fee is not established and must be confirmed with the clerk.
